examples.text: О, а вот и наш герой пришёл.
examples.trans: Oh, and here comes our hero.

examples.text: Мы сейчас нашему шефу помогаем.
examples.trans: We are helping our chef right now.

examples.text: Наша Катя пришла с байкерами в зал.
examples.trans: Our Katya came into the dining room with bikers.

meanings.note: Borrowed from French 'chef' (head, leader, from Latin 'caput'); in Russian kitchen culture 'шеф' is the standard form of address for the executive head chef.

examples.text: Мы сейчас нашему шефу помогаем.
examples.trans: We are helping our chef right now.

examples.text: Огромное вам спасибо за помощь, шеф!
examples.trans: Thank you so much for your help, Chef!

examples.text: Огромное спасибо, шеф!
examples.trans: Thank you so much, Chef!

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'могать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to help', paired with 'помочь'.

examples.text: Мы сейчас нашему шефу помогаем.
examples.trans: We are helping our chef right now.

examples.text: Помогайте Лаврову.
examples.trans: Help Lavrov.

examples.text: Я всегда помогаю соседям.
examples.trans: I always help the neighbours.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronominal determiner meaning 'some', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Бред какой-то.
examples.trans: What nonsense.

examples.text: Тебе звонил какой-то человек.
examples.trans: Some man called you.

examples.text: Бред какой-то. Но, с другой стороны, чем я рискую?
examples.trans: What nonsense. But on the other hand, what have I got to lose?

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('bad').

examples.text: Катя с каким-то плохим байкером связалась.
examples.trans: Katya got mixed up with some bad biker.

examples.text: А вот с тобой дела совсем плохо.
examples.trans: With you, however, things are really bad.

examples.text: Алло, скорая, тут человеку плохо, аппендицит, наверное!
examples.trans: Hello, ambulance, someone is sick here, probably appendicitis!

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'with a biker' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Собираю всякие байки на заказ.
examples.trans: I build all kinds of bikes to order.

examples.text: Ты была с этим байкером?
examples.trans: Were you with that biker?

examples.text: Катя с каким-то плохим байкером связалась.
examples.trans: Katya got mixed up with some bad biker.

meanings.en: to get in touch with, to contact
meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'вязаться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'got mixed up with', paired with 'связываться'.

examples.text: Я с вами свяжусь.
examples.trans: I will be in touch with you.

examples.text: Свяжитесь со мной завтра.
examples.trans: Contact me tomorrow.

examples.text: До свидания. Я с вами свяжусь.
examples.trans: Goodbye. I'll be in touch with you.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'so', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: У меня в молодости такой мотоцикл был.
examples.trans: I had a motorcycle like that in my youth.

examples.text: У меня такой в мастерской стоит.
examples.trans: I have one like that standing in my workshop.

examples.text: Девчонки меня так недавно назвали.
examples.trans: The girls recently gave me that name.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'what, that', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: А что у тебя за мастерская?
examples.trans: And what kind of workshop do you have?

examples.text: Вы что, знакомы, это мой отец!
examples.trans: Do you two know each other, this is my father!

examples.text: Привет, что ты мне названиваешь?
examples.trans: Hi, why do you keep calling me?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'come on', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

related.gloss: to give (the verb it comes from)

examples.text: Девчонки меня так недавно назвали.
examples.trans: The girls recently gave me that name.

examples.text: Иди давай, мы тебя ждём на улице.
examples.trans: Go on then, we are waiting for you outside.

examples.text: Давление, наверное, может, я дома отлежусь?
examples.trans: It is probably blood pressure, maybe I can rest at home?

meanings.en: to decide, to make up one's mind
meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to decide, to solve', paired with 'решить'.

examples.text: Как мы между собой конфликты решаем?
examples.trans: How do we settle conflicts among ourselves?

examples.text: Так что давай решай как-то сам, сынок.
examples.trans: So go ahead and work it out yourself somehow, son.

examples.text: Сами решайте, что делать.
examples.trans: Decide for yourselves what to do.

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Вчера как-то неудобно у нас получилось.
examples.trans: Things turned out rather awkwardly between us yesterday.

examples.text: Так что давай решай как-то сам, сынок.
examples.trans: So go ahead and work it out yourself somehow, son.

examples.text: Даже мне сейчас как-то стыдно.
examples.trans: Even I feel a bit ashamed right now.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'ынок'). Formed with a diminutive/expressive Slavic suffix adding warmth or small scale. Common masculine noun meaning 'son' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Так что давай решай как-то сам, сынок.
examples.trans: So go ahead and work it out yourself somehow, son.

examples.text: Нет, ты так хорошо ей подходишь, сынок!
examples.trans: No, you suit her so well, son!

examples.text: Сынок, иди домой!
examples.trans: Son, come home!
